what_happened.line: The Finance Committee voted unanimously to recommend approval of Article 6, the capital plan, as laid out in the draft.
The committee voted unanimously to defer Article 14, the sewer enterprise fund, to Town Meeting; the sewer commission had not yet voted on its revised budget.
The committee voted 4-1 to recommend approval of Article 21, the means-tested senior citizen property tax exemption petition.
The committee voted unanimously to recommend approval of Article 20, the historic homes survey, which funds a town-wide consultant survey with a reimbursement share.
The committee decided its annual report will be a separate factual document outside the warrant, with bullets on risks, and set a vote on the warrant for April 20.

why_it_matters: Article 6 sets which capital items the town funds; items below the funded line, such as a school pickup truck, McNally Park and cemetery turf, are not in this year's plan.
Article 21 would change who qualifies for a property tax exemption, so it is a vote residents will be asked to take at Town Meeting, and the 4-1 split shows the committee was not unanimous.
The sewer budget goes to Town Meeting without a committee recommendation, and sewer user charges and capital in it were still subject to a commission vote.
watch_next: April 20 Finance Committee meeting, kept as a public hearing, where the committee is to vote on the Town Meeting warrant.
The sewer commission's vote on its revised budget, which bears on Article 14.

reconciliation.summary: The four recorded votes agree on outcome, including the 4-1 split on Article 21, but the official minutes carry almost none of the dollar figures we heard. They also differ on who chaired, who was invited to a future meeting, and what Article 20 is.
